newsitem.title: UK: Beazer says firm second half marks recovery.
newsitem.headline: Beazer says firm second half marks recovery.

text.p: Beazer Homes Plc, the UK housebuilder, reported a fall in its annual pretax profits on Thursday but said that an improved second half performance had helped the group recover ground lost earlier in the year.
Pretax profits in the 12 months to June 30 were 46.5 million stg compared with 55.7 million a year ago.
The annual dividend was raised to 6 pence from 5.85 pence.
Chairman Victor Benjamin praised the results for achieving "one of our highest levels of completions," adding that house reservations in the current financial year were already up one third on 1995.

In his outlook, the chairman said "against a backdrop of increasing consumer confidence, trading is good," but he warned it was necessary to keep up the sales momentum this financial year, which will see a general election.
An election is due to be held by May 1997.
Looking at a breakdown of the results, Beazer completed 5,979 homes which generated turnover of 380.2 million stg versus 413.2 million.
Operating profit finished the year down 13 percent at 45.9 million stg, a rebound from the 22 percent decline seen in the first half.
New acquisition Charles Church contributed 35.3 million stg.
The group's average selling price for a home rose by three percent in the year to 63,300 stg, reflecting a minor change to the product mix and a lower level of social housing.
The group's land bank was 20,167 plots by the year end, with an average value of 12,900 stg per plot.
